# `silk/compress/lzma`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Decode complete LZMA-alone streams into caller-owned byte buffers.

## When to use
Use [`Lzma.decode`](#Lzma.impl.decode) for `.lzma` files with the 13-byte LZMA-alone header.
Use `silk.compress.lzma2.Lzma2` for raw LZMA2 chunks and `silk.compress.xz.Xz` for `.xz` files.

## Details
Decoding allocates probability tables through the ambient allocator. The output buffer also
holds dictionary history. Both known-size streams and streams with end markers are accepted.
Input must contain exactly one stream. There is no checksum; use an authenticated container
when integrity is required. Discard output after a failure.

Import as `Lzma` with `import silk.compress.lzma { Lzma }`.

### Associated function `decode`

```silk
pub effect fn decode(input: &[u8], output: &mut [u8], limits: DecodeLimits) -> Decoded
    ! OutOfMemoryError | DecodeError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Decodes one 13-byte-header LZMA-alone stream into the start of `output`.

#### Details
Allocates probability tables with the ambient allocator and uses `output` for dictionary
history. Known-size streams may omit the end marker; unknown-size streams must include it.
Returns the consumed and written lengths. Trailing bytes are rejected. LZMA has no checksum.

#### Errors
Fails with `DecodeError` for malformed or truncated data, trailing bytes, invalid distances,
size mismatches, or exhausted input, output, dictionary, or workspace limits. Output is not
verified on failure and must be discarded. Allocation failure raises `OutOfMemoryError`.
